Figure 3. Layer-wise token-drop analysis. Left: Schematic of the layer-wise token-drop probe, illustrating the information flow of
image-drop and action-drop. Right: Dropping Ahis at shallow depths (k<12) causes a much larger decline than dropping Vhis . Even if rich
visual information is retained, later layers cannot directly extract effective cues from Vhis without the action anchors. As k increases, the
action-drop curve rises toward the image-drop curve and the image–action drop curve converges rapidly.

Figure 4. Overview of our history context-aware optimization framework for building HiconAgent. HCPO improves both the sampling and
update phases of policy optimization by incorporating two key components: (1) Dynamic Context Sampling (DCS), which introduces
varied history lengths during training to encourage context-effective decision-making, and (2) Anchor-guided History Compression
(AHC), which adopts a dual-branch architecture where both branches share sampled responses and group-wise advantages. The compressed
branch is trained using policy gradients, aligned with the uncompressed branch via a history-enhanced alignment loss.

5. HiconAgent                                                        pose an exponential-biased distribution that mitigates train-
                                                                     ing collapse by gradually shifting the sampling toward larger

Figure 6. To illustrate HCPO’s enhancement in leveraging historical information, we present two scenarios: Left (Flight Booking) and Right
(Shopping Task). Our model correctly inputs Delhi by reasoning over historical context and selects Red Chief despite visual redundancy.
While the base model trained without HCPO misinterprets history and fails in both cases.

is successfully terminated, suggesting that HCPO strength-                                                     7. Conclusion
ens the model’s ability to maintain global sequence control
                                                                                                               In this paper, we present HiconAgent, a history-aware GUI
rather than overfitting to local step transitions. Improve-
                                                                                                               agent trained with History Context-aware Policy Optimiza-
ments are also evident in challenging categories such as
scroll, which demands exact direction prediction, and type,                                                    tion. Through extensive empirical investigations, we first
which often involves generating context-relevant input. Such                                                   revisited how history is utilized in GUI reinforcement learn-
findings highlight that our history-aware training paradigm                                                    ing agents. Our two key studies revealed that different de-
remains effective in scenarios where historical cues are es-                                                   cision steps prefer different history lengths and historical
                                                                                                               actions serve as information flow anchors. By pairing DCS
sential for accurate action generation.
                                                                                                               and AHC, our model outperforms larger models with fewer
                                                                                                               FLOPs. These results highlight HiconAgent as a practical
                                                                                                               path toward lightweight, high-performance GUI agents.
